newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil shares seen mixed amid corruption scandal.
newsitem.headline: Brazil shares seen mixed amid corruption scandal.

text.p: Brazil stocks are seen mixed Thursday as investors remain concerned about allegations that a government minister was linked to a cash-for-votes scam involving a re-election bill, brokers said.

On Wednesday, local shares nosedived after Folha de Sao Paulo newspaper alleged Communications Minister Sergio Motta was involved in the scandal in which five deputies were allegedly paid to vote for a bill allowing presidential re-election.

Motta denied any role in the vote-buying scheme but Folha reported today that Deputy Ronivon Santiago, who has allegedly admitted to selling his vote for money, said in another taped conversation that the minister granted him a television concession in exchange for his vote.
Analysts said investors are likely to be cautious, awaiting fresh developments in the case as opposition lawmakers are pressuring to set up a parliamentary inquiry into the scandal.
However, Wednesday's sharp drop, the biggest in a single session so far this year, could prompt players to look for some bargains, some brokers said.
They also Telebras first quarter earnings, although in line with market expectations, could encourage investors to buy the stock.
Late Wednesday, Telebras said it reported a net consolidated profit of 691 million reais in the first quarter.
